classes.name: Mandala Drawing w/ Nicole Stirling - 2 Days - $140
classes.description:
Mandala Drawing
2-Day Class | 3 Hours per Day
$140

Join artist and friend, Nicole Stirling, to learn the basics of drawing your own mandalas, starting at the roots with a compass, ruler, and protractor. Discover the joy of sacred geometry and the amazing things you can do with simply a compass and ruler. In this workshop, you’ll be creating your own mandala using these tools and basic drawing skills. This beginner-friendly workshop guides you through the full process - from designing and drawing a simple mandala to finishing it with ink and color.

Day 1:
You’ll begin with learning the ‘mandala map’ basics, and a primer on using your new geometry tools. After getting comfortable with your tools and drawing your map you’ll learn the basics of mandala design including symmetry and pattern building.

Day 2:
Transform your design into a vibrant work of art! Using colored pencils, ink, or markers you’ll bring your mandala to life with color while learning tips for clean lines, blending, and long-lasting results.
 
All materials are provided, and no artistic experience is needed. You’ll leave with your own set of mandala drawing tools, and a beautiful piece of artwork that will be ready to frame and display in your space, or gift to someone you love.

Create something colorful, calming, and uniquely yours!
 
Ages: 12 to adult.
Maximum 12 students.
 
Artist Bio
Nicole Stirling is a vibrant visual artist known for her love of bold color, intricate detail, and geometric pattern. Born and raised in Lake Tahoe, California, Nicole draws deep inspiration from the magical, forested landscapes of her home - places she has spent countless days exploring and observing.
 
From a young age she was enrolled in local art classes, experimenting with landscape painting, clay, and ink drawings. Though she majored in music in college, Nicole consistently pursued her passion for visual art, taking painting and drawing classes alongside her studies. Her early college painting courses included woodshop labs, where she learned to build her own stretcher bars; a skill that empowered her to create large-scale oil paintings and step fully into her identity as an artist.

Nicole has long been captivated by circular forms and began developing mandala-inspired works featuring concentric patterns, sacred geometry, and global motifs. Her mandalas incorporate natural elements and psychedelic designs, blending structure and spontaneity in a deeply meditative process. She sees both the act of creation and the final piece as opportunities for mindful exploration and the opportunity to slow down.
 
Nicole is also the owner of Chickadee Art Collective in Kings Beach - a gallery and retail shop showcasing artists from the Tahoe, Truckee, and Reno areas.

Wood Shop 101 $145
2 Days - 3.5 hours each
 
Wood Shop 101 is designed to help you cultivate the skills, knowledge, and attitudes necessary to start and troubleshoot basic woodshop projects.

You are not expected to have any prior woodshop experience and the information should be a helpful refresher for anyone looking to get back into the woodshop. This course is designed to give you hands-on experience with the woodshop power tools and machines and work on a project. 

During the 2nd session of this course, you will demonstrate all that you have learned by creating a wood carry tote that can be used for beverages, gardening, etc.

  • Miter Saw
  • Bandsaw
  • Basic hand tools
  • Belt / Disc Sander — Orbital sander (optional)
  • Drill Press

This course counts as a safety checkout to use these tools as a member.

You will also learn how to:

-Practice strategies for safe making
-Be a steward of the woodshop
-Identify basic characteristics of wood (hardness, grain, cost, etc.) and their use in different projects
-Identity appropriate woodshop tools for different needs (prep, dimensioning)
-Summarize and use the design process to create a basic project
-Use appropriate tools of the woodshop to prepare, clean, and dimension wood for a project
-Fasten or connect multiple pieces of wood
-Clean up thoroughly after using the woodshop

Two sessions, 7 hours of instruction.

Ages 12 and above. All youth under the age of 16 must be chaperoned by an adult also taking the class. 
Maximum 4 students.

No previous woodworking skills are necessary.

Butcher Blocks for Beginners $115 all materials included
2 sessions
 
This two-day class will walk you through all the steps in making a beautiful butcher block cutting board. 
 
This class will provide an introduction to the Wood Shop using the Butcher Block cutting board as a project.
 
The course will cover the different types of wood you can use and address the difference and between domestic and exotic, light and dark wood species.
 
You will be instructed on how to prepare your wood, including the cutting, milling, and attachment.
 
The 2nd class will be focused on finishing: planner action, orbit sander, mineral oil, cleaning, how to attach handles, maintenance, and a short quiz about wood species.

The material used for the class: dark walnut, redwood, poplar, aspen, maple, mahogany, white oak, and possibly cedar and hickory.
 
Specs for butcher block: roughly 12" by 22 "and roughly 1 1/4 thickness.
